protections: Request-time policy gate: call_aws_helper must obtain a DENY/ELICIT/ALLOW decision from check_security_policy (denyList, elicitList, READ_OPERATIONS_ONLY_MODE, REQUIRE_MUTATION_CONSENT) before dispatching any command (src/aws-api-mcp-server/awslabs/aws_api_mcp_server/server.py:321-341; src/aws-api-mcp-server/awslabs/aws_api_mcp_server/core/aws/service.py:92-119; src/aws-api-mcp-server/awslabs/aws_api_mcp_server/core/security/policy.py:109-139).

Startup fail-closed: main() must not start serving when the read-only operations index cannot be built (src/aws-api-mcp-server/awslabs/aws_api_mcp_server/server.py:440-445; src/aws-api-mcp-server/awslabs/aws_api_mcp_server/core/metadata/read_only_operations_list.py:143-145 and 47-59).

Policy-file integrity: when ~/.aws/aws-api-mcp/mcp-security-policy.json exists but cannot be read or parsed, the deny/elicit lists must not silently become empty (src/aws-api-mcp-server/awslabs/aws_api_mcp_server/core/security/policy.py:56-87).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The else branch reads as a deliberate degraded policy (deny everything in read-only mode, otherwise request consent) and repo tests patch READ_OPERATIONS_INDEX to None while still expecting the command to execute (tests/test_server.py:188-205, 236-254), so the branch looks intended rather than like the policy being skipped.

The failure is only logged as a warning, the repo test explicitly says main() should not raise, just log the warning (tests/test_server.py:30-42), and aborting breaks offline starts because building the index performs a network fetch (read_only_operations_list.py:53-57).

The policy file is optional user config: absence is explicitly tolerated (policy.py:60-65) and a test asserts an unparseable file is handled gracefully with empty deny/elicit lists (tests/test_security_policy.py:105-138); the advisory names only the read-only operations index, so a solver can call this intended tolerance.

The customization table is shipped inside the package with every entry populated (core/security/aws_api_customization.json) and a test asserts a missing api_calls key loads as an empty list (tests/test_security_policy.py:187-205); an empty list is not reachable from user input, so the ALLOW-on-no-decisions branch can be called latent rather than exploitable.

Injection-room sibling (a schema/coercion step wired into _load_policy would sit here; not a planted change at this commit): the underlying weakness is already present because set(policy['denyList']) and set(policy['elicitList']) have no type check (policy.py:76, 80), so a string value silently becomes a set of characters and never matches; the documented format is an array (README.md:381-389), so a solver can dismiss a wrong-typed value as user error instead of a fail-open.

Injection-room sibling (a second executor calling interpret_command or execute_awscli_customization directly; not present at this commit): a new executor added next to call_aws would look self-contained, and the repo tests already call those functions with mocks (tests/test_server.py:165-205), so the missing gate would be easy to overlook.

Injection-room sibling (an on-disk cache of the read-only index that falls back to an empty index; not present at this commit): it would look like availability work, and the class already tolerates per-service cache misses (read_only_operations_list.py:89-93), so an empty index reads as nothing cached rather than as enforcement data missing.

Injection-room sibling (a configurable policy-file path read from the environment; not present at this commit): it would sit beside the other env options (config.py:167-195) and inherit the same optional-config tolerance, so an unset or wrong path reads as no policy configured instead of as failed enforcement data.

masking: T2's swallow is what makes T1 reachable: fixing only T2 (raise at startup) removes the production path to READ_OPERATIONS_INDEX=None, so a solver can believe the fail-open is gone while call_aws_helper still executes any command when the index is None (server.py:323, 332-341).
Fixing only T1 (deny on None) leaves T2 an availability and robustness bug and hides that the server still starts with no enforcement data (server.py:441-445).

conflicts.what: A fail-closed startup that aborts when the read-only index cannot be built contradicts an offline disk-cache design that starts with an empty index; the latter recreates the same empty-enforcement-data, keep-serving fail-open (server.py:441-445 vs read_only_operations_list.py:95-106).

Both are missing-security-data decisions but need opposite defaults: T1 must deny when the read-only index is unavailable (server.py:332-341), while a default install with no policy file must keep allowing every operation (policy.py:60-65); one shared fail-closed helper over both would refuse the documented default install.

fairness_risks: A default install with no ~/.aws/aws-api-mcp/mcp-security-policy.json must still start and allow every operation (policy.py:60-65; README.md:377-389); a fail-closed rule for a policy file that failed to load must not treat absence as failure.

With a valid index, READ_OPERATIONS_ONLY_MODE=True must still allow read-only operations and REQUIRE_MUTATION_CONSENT=True must still elicit only for mutations (policy.py:132-136); a blanket deny must not replace the normal decision path.
Customizations and help operations must still dispatch after a successful gate (server.py:343-359); fail-closed must apply only to the missing-index state, not to every command.

A legitimate read-only command such as aws s3 ls is denied under the required fail-closed behaviour when the index failed to load, and startup now depends on a live fetch of the service-reference document (read_only_operations_list.py:53-57), so offline and air-gapped starts break.

The repo tests encode the current vulnerable fallback: test_main_read_operations_index_load_failure asserts main() does not raise (tests/test_server.py:30-42) and several tests patch READ_OPERATIONS_INDEX=None and expect execution (tests/test_server.py:188-205, 236-254, 257-313); a correct fix must change these expectations.

design.why: T1 and T2 are two independent fix sites of the published advisory: a solver who only turns main()'s warning into a raise (server.py:441-445) leaves call_aws_helper executing commands whenever the index is None (server.py:332-341), and a solver who only denies in the request path leaves the server able to start with no enforcement data. T3 is a real, independent upstream fail-open in the same feature (policy.py:67-85) with the strongest reason to dismiss (optional config plus a repo test asserting graceful degradation), giving a deepseek-type xhard trap around the M11 absent-vs-invalid coupled value. Together the three span startup, request dispatch and per-request policy loading, each with a different dismissal, and they include a mimo-type (T2, producer off path) and a deepseek-type (T3). A two-trap design would cover only the advisory; T4 (empty api_calls proxy, policy.py:167-211) is a weaker fourth because the shipped customization table always populates api_calls and user input cannot reach it, and the README subprocess denylist is not a trap at all because those custom operations are absent from ALLOWED_CUSTOM_OPERATIONS and rejected at parse time (parser.py:362-378, 522-523).
